Documents the three-layer fix, the --max-budget-usd fail-closed semantics, and a macOS /var symlink gotcha.","source":"claude-code:turbo-rig","body_html":"

Problem

Nightly loop cost kept climbing even with minimal new work. Root cause: every headless claude -p invocation persists its own session transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/, keyed by an encoding of the working directory. The loop ran from $TMPDIR/loopwatch.XXXXXX, a fresh temp dir each night, so each run created a new project dir (e.g. -private-var-folders-...-T-loopwatch-a1B2c3) containing the entire input bundle it was fed — a one-word test answer produced a 231 KB transcript. The collector's glob ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl then picked up that transcript the following night, so night N+1 re-ingested night N's input: cost compounded and stale content got re-mined indefinitely.

Fix: three layers

  1. CLI flag: pass --no-session-persistence. Verified on claude 2.1.283 that no project dir is created at all when set.
  2. Fixed run directory: always run from a stable path, ~/.local/state/loopwatch/run, instead of a fresh temp dir per run. Exclude its corresponding encoded project dir from collection (every non-alphanumeric char in the path becomes -), plus any dir suffixed -loopwatch-run, and the older v0.1 loopwatch-XXXXXX mktemp-style dirs, for backward compatibility. Tradeoff: a fixed run dir means runs must be serialized — acceptable here because the existing mkdir-based lock already enforces that.
  3. Watermark filtering: as a last-resort net, drop any transcript line whose cwd field equals the run dir. This catches the case where the project dir gets moved or renamed and layer 2's name-based exclusion misses it.

Budget enforcement semantics

--max-budget-usd is actively enforced mid-call: a cap of 0.05 on a call that would have cost 0.066 returned is_error:true with exit code 1 (the call did not silently truncate or downgrade). Decision: treat a budget hit as a failed run, not a partial success — hold watermarks at their prior value and record a ledger row with skipped_reason=budget_exceeded. Advancing watermarks on a budget-killed run would permanently lose the un-ingested delta; failing closed lets the same delta retry next run.

Verification

claude -p 'Reply with exactly: ok' --model haiku --output-format json --no-session-persistence

Confirmed no project directory appears under ~/.claude/projects/ after this call.

Gotchas

  • On macOS, /var is a symlink to /private/var, so the encoded project-dir name computed from a logical path can differ from what actually gets created on disk. This is why the exclusion logic matches on a directory-name suffix pattern rather than an exact computed encoding.
  • A one-word response can still produce a six-figure-byte transcript, because the full input bundle is embedded in the persisted session, not just the reply.
